what_it_is.prose: The Centre for Military Airworthiness & Certification (CEMILAC) is the Defence Research & Development Organisation laboratory that acts as India's military airworthiness certification authority, established in 1995 and headquartered in Bengaluru. Every system, Line Replaceable Unit (LRU), component, material and software item used on Indian military airborne platforms — fixed-wing aircraft, helicopters, UAVs, aerostats and parachutes — must be certified by CEMILAC. It operates a 'concurrent certification' model in which airworthiness assurance proceeds alongside design and development, and it issues the type certificate (type approval) that grants authority to produce or manufacture a product under government inspection and the supervision of a designated Regional Centre for Military Airworthiness (RCMA). CEMILAC runs a network of regional centres (14 reported) co-located with design and production agencies across India, and administers a Design Organisation Approval Scheme (DOAS) that recognises design houses with an established Design Assurance System (requiring AS9100 approval as a prerequisite). Its clearances underpin India's indigenous aircraft programmes: CEMILAC issued Initial Operational Clearance (IOC) for the LCA Tejas and the ALH Dhruv, and cleared bio-jet fuel (Bio-ATF) use in the AN-32. It has launched an e-Certification portal (cemilac.drdo.gov.in) to streamline registration and submissions. As a certification authority rather than a manufacturer, CEMILAC is a foundational, if less visible, node of India's military-aerospace ecosystem — nothing indigenous flies with the armed forces without its clearance.

deployments_procurement.summary: CEMILAC does not procure or manufacture; its 'output' is airworthiness certification of India's military aircraft and airborne systems. Its documented clearances include Initial Operational Clearance for the LCA Tejas and ALH Dhruv and Bio-ATF clearance for the AN-32, and it certifies the systems, LRUs, materials and software across DRDO/HAL/industry aircraft programmes.

import_dependencies.summary: As a certification authority, CEMILAC has no manufacturing supply chain of its own. Its dependency is methodological: Indian military airworthiness standards and processes are partly harmonised with international frameworks (US FAR, UK DEF-STAN, MIL standards) and AS9100 for design organisations, but the certification authority itself is fully sovereign.

faq.question: What is CEMILAC and why does it matter?
faq.answer: CEMILAC is DRDO's military airworthiness certification authority, established in 1995 in Bengaluru. It certifies and qualifies every Indian military airborne platform and every system, component, material and software item used on them. Nothing indigenous — fighters, helicopters, UAVs, aerostats — enters armed-forces service without CEMILAC's airworthiness clearance, which makes it a foundational gatekeeper of India's military-aerospace ecosystem.

faq.question: What has CEMILAC certified?
faq.answer: CEMILAC issued Initial Operational Clearance (IOC) for the LCA Tejas and the ALH Dhruv helicopter, and cleared bio-jet fuel (Bio-ATF) for use in the AN-32 transport aircraft. It issues type certificates (type approval) that authorise production under government inspection and the supervision of its Regional Centres for Military Airworthiness (RCMA), of which about 14 operate across India, and administers a Design Organisation Approval Scheme requiring AS9100.
